## Body

Coder, chainglass nav wave 1 (2026-11-12): landed ctx-max 819b43229 + fix 69031952b, nav-progress 574d871ca + fix f23b70f58. Lessons that cost me time:

- Browser proofs must never reach Jordan's tmux. The web app's terminal overlay attaches with `tmux new-session -A`; after a client-side navigation its session resets to the workspace default, so a spare-port server on the default tmux server attached a headless client to Jordan's live `chainglass` session (window-size=latest, so it can resize his windows). Use the wave rule: `tmux -L <slug>`, or a private, existing, chmod-700 TMUX_TMPDIR with TMUX and TMUX_PANE unset, proven by `tmux display -p '#{socket_path}'` first. NEVER `tmux kill-server`: tmux 3.6a silently falls back to the default socket when TMUX_TMPDIR does not exist, which killed the whole fleet twice.
- Faking pij seats for a terminal proof: the sidecar reads `/v1/cards` via PIJ_RS_ADDR + PIJ_RS_STATE_DIR (needs a `daemon.key` file). A 20-line Bun server returning `{ok,command,v,data:{cards}}` with real pane ids and pids from a private tmux server works. The sidecar also needs TERMINAL_WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS for a non-3000 port.
- Clamped display values are not ranking keys: rank by the raw ratio and clamp only for display (quokka P2 on fullestContext).
- If you compare URLs to decide "a navigation started", compare in the same canonical form the end signal uses (sorted URLSearchParams); `%20` vs `+` otherwise leaves the bar stuck (quokka P2).
- Next 16 `useRouter()` returns a per-component memoized copy of push/replace: patching the router singleton does not reach existing callers. Wrap at call sites (`useProgressRouter`).
- Screenshots for a deliverable must come from the landed head's build, not a pre-rebase build; say which build each image came from.
- `git worktree add` does not copy apps/web/.env.local (an APFS clone does). Nothing NEXT_PUBLIC_ is in it, so builds are unaffected, but a reviewer serving the build needs `--env-file` pointing at main's.
- Check a published deliverable for leftover placeholders before publishing (I shipped `{SHA}`/`{FFT}` once; republished as -2).
- Full runs are serialized by the prime; a slot can be reassigned mid-run, so kill your run promptly and say what state it left (e.g. a rebuilt .next).
